prompt_text: My air conditioning needs fixing in Phoenix. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
I can give specific company names, but to pick the best local options for you I need two quick details: 1) your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and 2) is this an emergency (no cool air right now) or a non-urgent repair/maintenance? If you provide those I’ll give a short, prioritized list of local companies to call and why each is a good fit.

Meanwhile, here are three reputable companies that commonly serve Phoenix and why you might call them now (these are good starting points if you want names immediately):

- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning
  - Why: Large regional presence, offers same-day service and 24/7 emergency dispatch in many areas, technicians often NATE-certified, and they provide maintenance plans and system warranties. Good if you want predictable service and a maintenance contract.

- ARS/Rescue Rooter (Heating & Air division)
  - Why: National company with established local branches. They handle emergencies, replacements, and have wide parts access—useful in extreme heat when parts may be needed quickly.

- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (One Hour / Benjamin Franklin family)
  - Why: Known for punctuality guarantees and flat-rate pricing in many markets, often offers diagnostic fees applied toward repairs/installation, and tends to be responsive for next-day or same-day service.

What I’ll do if you give your ZIP code:
- Provide 4–6 specific local HVAC companies (mix of reputable national branches and top-rated local contractors) with short reasons (response time, specialties, reviews, licensing) and a recommended first call.
- Include one emergency-only option (24/7) and one small local shop (often cheaper for repairs/warranty work).

Quick checklist and script to use when you call any company (helps avoid surprises):
- Confirm they are licensed with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ask for license number) and insured.
- Ask if techs are NATE-certified and EPA 608 certified.
- Ask if they charge a service/diagnostic fee and whether that fee is credited to repairs.
- Ask estimated arrival window, same-day availability, and any after-hours/emergency surcharge.
- Ask about parts warranty and labor warranty.
- Get a written estimate before work starts (itemized: parts, labor, refrigerant if applicable).
- If installation is needed, ask about permits and energy-efficiency rebates.

Call script (copy/paste):
“Hi — I have [brief problem: e.g., no cooling / AC blowing warm air / leaking refrigerant]. Are you available for a same-day service call? What is your service/diagnostic fee, and will that fee be applied to any repair? Are your technicians NATE-certified and do you carry Arizona ROC license #? What is your ETA for a service visit, and do you provide a written estimate before beginning work?”

If you share your ZIP code and whether it’s an emergency, I’ll return specific, prioritized company names in your immediate area with reasons and one to call first.
